question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity:

$$
1-{tanh}^{2}⁡\theta ={sech}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Setting $\theta =3x-2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{tanh}^{2}⁡(3x-2) & ={sech}^{2}⁡(3x-2) \\ {tanh}^{2}⁡(3x-2) & =1-{sech}^{2}⁡(3x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{tanh}^{2}⁡(3x-2)}{3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int (1-{sech}^{2}⁡(3x-2))\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int 1\cdot \text{d}x-\frac{1}{3}\int {sech}^{2}⁡(3x-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x}{3}-\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x-2)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
